newsitem.title: UK: BG up as official trade starts, Centrica off.
newsitem.headline: BG up as official trade starts, Centrica off.

text.p: Trading in the demerged shares on British Gas Plc got underway on Monday with shares in BG Plc, which owns the company's pipeline network and its exploration operations, rising while trading arm Centrica Plc fell.
BG shares were up 4p at 174-1/2 by 0830 GMT compared with the close of "grey market" or unofficial trading in the stock on Friday, while Centrica shares were down 3p at 72-1/2.

Centrica was stronger last week than some analysts expected and the stock was confirmed as a member of the FTSE 100 index, yet the influential Financial Times Lex column on Saturday suggested investors should switch out of Centrica and into BG.
Lex said BG was worth 220p a share on the basis of a valuation of its pipeline network and its "upstream" businesses, yet valued Centrica at as little as 25p.
"Certainly BG looks better value," the FT said, "investors should sell the one and buy the other."
Centrica faces the loss of its monopoly in the supply of gas to UK households next year with the opening of the entire UK gas market to competition.
Trials of the open market for natural gas in the South West of England started last April have so far resulted in some 20 percent of customers deserting to rivals.
